Sabbath Rest
săb´băth rĕst
n. phrase (the ceasing appointed at creation, commanded at Sinai, fulfilled in Christ, and remaining for the people of God)
Hebrew shabbath, from shabath, to cease — not primarily to be refreshed but simply to stop. Hebrews coins a Greek word for it, sabbatismos, a sabbath-keeping, used once in the New Testament.

Biblical Definition

The sabbath rest begins at creation: “And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made” (Gen 2:2). It is commanded at Sinai on that ground: “Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy… for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth… and rested the seventh day” (Exo 20:8–11). Its purpose is stated by the Lord: “The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath” (Mar 2:27). Its substance is Christ: the ordinances “are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ” (Col 2:17). And a rest remains: “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God” (Heb 4:9).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines sabbath as the day which God appointed to be observed by the Jews as a day of rest from all secular labor, and to be kept holy and consecrated to his service; and notes it is also called the Lord's day, observed by Christians on the first day of the week.

expand to see more

SABBATH, n. The day which God appointed to be observed by the Jews as a day of rest from all secular labor or employments, and to be kept holy and consecrated to his service and worship.

This day is called the sabbath, or day of rest; and the seventh day of the week was thus consecrated.

2. The day observed by christians as holy time, is the first day of the week, in commemoration of our Savior's resurrection; and hence called the Lord's day.

3. Intermission of pain, effort, sorrow, or the like; as, a sabbath of the mind.

Key Scripture

Gen 2:2 — "And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made."

Exo 20:8 — "Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy."

Mar 2:27 — "And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:"

Col 2:17 — "Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ."

Heb 4:9 — "There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God."

Modern Corruption

The day is defended and the rest is never taken, or the rest is claimed and the day is despised; and the Lord's quarrel was with people who kept it scrupulously.

expand to see more

Mark 2:27 was spoken in a dispute about disciples pulling ears of corn on the sabbath, and it reverses the whole rabbinic frame: the sabbath was made for man, not man for the sabbath. It is a gift before it is an obligation, given to a people who had just come out of a country where slaves worked without a day off — and Deuteronomy makes that the reason: remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt. Every sabbath argument that ends with people more burdened than they began has lost the verse.

The Reformed have divided on the day and this dictionary states its position plainly: the fourth commandment is moral and abiding, its substance is a day in seven consecrated to God, and its Christian observance is the first day, in commemoration of the resurrection — which is Webster's own account and the confessional one. What must not follow is the elaboration Christ opposed. The Pharisees had built a fence of rules around the day until healing a withered hand inside it became a crime, and He answered them by healing the hand.

Hebrews 4:9 keeps the doctrine from terminating on a calendar. There remaineth a rest to the people of God, and the word is sabbatismos, a sabbath-keeping still ahead. The weekly day is a rehearsal of something not yet possessed, which is why it is kept with rest and worship rather than with mere abstention; and it is also why Colossians 2:17 can call the ordinances a shadow and say the body is of Christ without abolishing the observance. A shadow proves a solid object. The Christian keeps the day looking backward at a finished work and forward at a rest that has not begun.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew shabath (H7673), to cease, rest; shabbath (H7676), sabbath; Greek sabbatismos (G4520), a sabbath-keeping; skia (G4639), a shadow.

expand to see more

Hebrew shabath (H7673) — to cease, desist; Genesis 2:2–3, Exodus 31:17, Joshua 5:12.

Greek sabbatismos (G4520) — a sabbath rest, a keeping of sabbath; Hebrews 4:9 only.

Greek skia…soma (G4639, G4983) — shadow…body; Colossians 2:17, Hebrews 8:5, 10:1.

Usage

"“The sabbath was made for man” — a gift before an obligation."

"“A shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ” — and a shadow proves a solid."

"“There remaineth therefore a rest” — still ahead."
